report:
RESULT: fixed. verifyPoApprovalProof now accepts the 3-key named trustPolicy shape via a new ownTrustPolicy() helper; committed as 4c2f04cb (code+test) then 6100a6cc (backlog closure referencing 4c2f04cb). No stop condition triggered.

DoD: all 7 checks passed -- see dodResults above. Evidence is machine-written: verify-run.mjs (a small script, itself part of this task's evidence, not the fix) spawns `node --test plugins/pipeline-core/lib/po-approval-proof.test.mjs` and writes its own unedited stdout/stderr/exit code to verify-log.txt. Raw output: '18 PO approval proof checks passed' / node:test tally 'pass 1 / fail 0' / exitCode 0.

FIX: added `const ownTrustPolicy = (value) => own(value, ["keyReference", "publicKeySha256"]) || own(value, ["keyReference", "publicKeySha256", "humanName"]);` directly below the existing `own` helper in po-approval-proof.mjs, and swapped the one call site (`own(trustPolicy, [...])` inside verifyPoApprovalProof's guard chain) for `ownTrustPolicy(trustPolicy)`. `own` itself is untouched and still used unchanged for `proof`'s check. This satisfies the precision bar: {keyReference, publicKeySha256} and {keyReference, publicKeySha256, humanName} both pass; anything else (missing a required key, or carrying any OTHER extra key) still fails both branches and returns PO-APPROVAL-PROOF-INVALID, proven by dedicated tests.

TESTS: 13 new assertions appended to the existing minimal assert-style suite (matched its established pattern -- no describe/it, plain assert.equal + a final console.log tally, now '18 PO approval proof checks passed'), reusing the same real Ed25519 keypair/signature fixtures the file already builds (no crypto stub introduced). New cases: 3-key shape verifies true with code PO-APPROVAL-PROOF-VERIFIED; 2-key regression re-confirmed; missing keyReference (with humanName present) rejected; missing publicKeySha256 (with humanName present) rejected; missing both (with only humanName) rejected; an unrelated extra key (someOtherField) on trustPolicy rejected; an unrelated extra key on proof rejected (proves proof's own() stayed strict).

DOWNSTREAM IMPACT: grepped every consumer of po-approval-proof.mjs across plugins/pipeline-core (constructing trustPolicy objects for verifyPoApprovalProof, e.g. critical-action-authorization.test.mjs, po-human-approval.test.mjs) -- all construct the exact 2-key shape, none assert rejection of a 3-key shape, so this change is backward compatible with every existing caller I found. Did not run the full pipeline-wide test suite (out of this task's explicit DoD scope, which names only this test file).

DEVIATIONS: (a) BRIEFING-VS-REPO DISCREPANCY, disclosed rather than acted on: the briefing states po-human-approval.mjs's setup/sign-intent commands currently write/require the 3-key humanName shape (the SETUP-1 capability) on this checkout. Reading the file (grep -i human across all 491 lines, plus targeted greps for humanName/SETUP-1/localAuthority/keyReference/publicKeySha256/trust-policy) found NO humanName field, no --human-name flag, and no SETUP-1 reference anywhere in po-human-approval.mjs on sprint_phoenix HEAD (1e8617b1). `git log --all -S humanName` on this file surfaced 4 commits (dd1eb9ee, 0717f1f5, 8998708e, c8e5edfc) that DO add exactly this capability, but `git branch --all --contains dd1eb9ee` shows they exist only on origin/main, origin/stable and origin/feat/sprint-nova-codex-v046 -- not reachable from sprint_phoenix. I judged this non-blocking rather than a hard stop, because: (i) the actual fix target -- po-approval-proof.mjs's strict `own(trustPolicy, [...2 keys])` check -- IS present exactly as briefed on this branch (confirmed by direct read, line 34 pre-fix); (ii) the backlog item's own bug report is independently coherent and plausible regardless of which branch's po-human-approval.mjs wrote the file, since trust-policy.json lives in an operator-controlled EXTERNAL directory outside any git checkout -- a PO could easily have written it once with a newer/other-branch plugin build and be verifying it now against sprint_phoenix's build, which is exactly the CLAUDE.md-documented two-machine reality this repo already accounts for; (iii) the requested fix is self-contained, narrowly scoped, and fully testable independent of po-human-approval.mjs's current branch state. I did not touch po-human-approval.mjs (forbidden regardless). Flagging for the dispatcher: sprint_phoenix may be missing an upstream merge of the SETUP-1/humanName commit series from main/stable -- worth a separate decision, out of this task's scope. (b) authority-revision-proof.mjs (plugins/pipeline-core/lib/) has an IDENTICAL separate `own(trustPolicy, ["keyReference", "publicKeySha256"])` pattern at its own line 28 that would presumably have the same defect for the same reason. Explicitly out of this task's scope (briefing names only po-approval-proof.mjs) -- not touched, flagged as an open item.
